title: Crossflow Cooling Tower Repair and Maintenance
lead: Inspection, repair and maintenance for industrial crossflow towers, from water distribution and fill to louvers, structure and fan drives.
overview: In a crossflow tower, water falls through fill while air moves horizontally across it. Uneven distribution, damaged louvers, fouled fill or structural wear can reduce the cooling delivered by the whole cell. ICS inspects the connected systems before recommending a repair.
principles: Distribution
Water moves through the hot-water basin and down through the fill. Blocked orifices can leave part of the fill dry.
Airflow
Air enters through the louvers and travels across the falling water before leaving through the fan stack.
Where to inspect
Fill, louvers, basin condition, structure and mechanical equipment all affect the result.
services: Hot-water basins and distribution
Inspect and repair blocked or damaged distribution components so water reaches the fill evenly.
Fill media
Replace old, clogged, scaled or damaged fill where it reduces heat rejection.
Louvers, casing and drift eliminators
Repair damaged air inlets and casing; replace worn eliminators to address water loss.
Cold-water basin
Inspect for debris, leakage, corrosion and damage affecting flow.
Structure and fan deck
Repair or replace damaged supports, framing, decks and panels.
Mechanical equipment
Inspect fan blades, drives, gearboxes, shafts and bearings for wear or vibration.
signsTitle: Signs your crossflow tower needs repair
signs: Cold-water temperature above the expected duty
Uneven water pattern or dry fill sections
supportTitle: Keeping a crossflow tower in condition
support: Routine inspection and planned maintenance help expose water-distribution, airflow and structural problems before they become a larger outage.
decision: ICS can compare a targeted repair with a wider upgrade or rebuild when the condition of the tower makes a single-component replacement insufficient.
faq: Can ICS inspect an existing crossflow tower?
Yes. A site inspection establishes the condition of the fill, distribution, structure and mechanical equipment before a scope is proposed.
Does every problem require a rebuild?
No. The right scope depends on the cause, affected components and remaining condition of the tower.
How do I request a repair assessment?
Use the existing ICS request-a-quote flow and share the tower make, model, duty and any inspection records available.
closing: Find out what is happening inside your crossflow tower.

title: Counterflow Cooling Tower Repair and Maintenance
lead: Repair and maintenance for the spray system, fill, drift eliminators, structure and drives inside an industrial counterflow tower.
overviewTitle: Why counterflow towers need a different repair approach
overview: In a counterflow tower, water moves down through fill while air rises in the opposite direction. Distribution and fill problems may be difficult to see from outside the cell. ICS checks the internal systems before selecting parts and repair work.
principles: Distribution
Water is delivered through headers and nozzles onto the fill; coverage across the cell matters.
Airflow
Air enters below and moves upward through the falling water and fill.
Where to inspect
Nozzles, laterals, fill, eliminators, basin and drives should be assessed as one operating system.
services: Spray distribution
Inspect headers, laterals and nozzles for blockage, leakage or damage.
Fill and supports
Repair support defects and replace fouled or damaged fill.
Drift eliminators
Replace worn or displaced sections that allow water carryover.
Structure and basin
Repair damaged casing, framing, decking and cold-water-basin areas.
Fan deck and stack
Inspect the deck and airflow path for structural or fit problems.
Mechanical drives
Check fans, hubs, gearboxes, shafts, motors and bearings when vibration or wear is reported.
signsTitle: Warning signs in a counterflow tower
signs: Cooling performance falling at a similar load
Water carryover at the fan discharge
Motor current, vibration or noise changing
supportTitle: Keeping a counterflow tower in condition
support: Planned internal inspections are important where the spray system and fill are hidden from normal view.
decision: Where several systems have deteriorated, ICS can help compare a contained repair with a larger upgrade or replacement scope.
faq: Can ICS repair a tower built by another manufacturer?
ICS assesses industrial towers and their installed components before recommending a suitable scope.
Should blocked fill be replaced?
That decision follows inspection of the fill, distribution system, support condition and water quality.
What should I send with an enquiry?
Tower identification, operating duty, photographs and any prior inspection reports help scope the request.
closing: Find out what is happening inside your counterflow tower.

title: Wet, Hybrid, and Dry Cooling Tower
lead: One service conversation for wet, hybrid and dry industrial cooling equipment, with the repair scope matched to how the installation rejects heat.
overviewTitle: One team for every type of cooling
overview: Wet, hybrid and dry configurations use different combinations of water, airflow and heat-exchange surfaces. ICS checks the installed arrangement and the condition of its mechanical and structural components before recommending maintenance or repair.
principles: Wet / evaporative
Water and airflow work together to remove heat through evaporation.
Dry
Heat is transferred to air without the same evaporative water path.
Hybrid
The installed system combines operating modes or components; the site configuration determines the inspection scope.
servicesTitle: Wet, hybrid and dry cooling tower repair services
services: Fill and water distribution
Inspect wet-side media and distribution where fitted.
Drift eliminators and air inlets
Check eliminators, louvers and the airflow path.
Structure, casing and supports
Identify damage and repair components affected by the operating environment.
Tube bundles and coils
Review heat-exchange surfaces where the installed system uses them.
Fans and drive systems
Investigate mechanical wear, vibration and airflow problems.
Water-side controls
Assess the related basin, distribution and operating components as applicable.
signsTitle: What we check on every tower
signs: Heat rejection no longer meeting duty
Leaks from coils, basin or casing
supportTitle: Hybrid cooling tower maintenance and site support
support: The maintenance plan should follow the equipment actually installed, its operating mode and its observed condition.
decision: When one repair cannot restore the required duty, ICS can review whether a wider upgrade or replacement better fits the site.
faq: Can ICS assess a hybrid cooling system?
Yes. The first step is to identify the installed configuration and collect the operating and condition evidence.
Is the same maintenance work used for wet and dry systems?
No. The service scope follows the components and operating mode present on site.
Can parts be included in the quotation?
The request can cover identified replacement parts together with the repair scope.
closing: Get one repair plan for your whole site.

title: Low Drift Solutions for Industrial Cooling Towers
lead: Find where water loss is occurring, then inspect, clean or replace the drift eliminators and tower components involved.
overview: Drift is water carried out in the tower exhaust. Damaged or poorly seated eliminators, distribution problems and airflow conditions may contribute to avoidable loss. ICS inspects the affected tower before recommending corrective work.
principles: Capture
Eliminator passages change the air path so entrained droplets can be separated.
Return
Captured water drains back toward the tower rather than leaving with the exhaust.
Airflow
Fit and condition matter: gaps, fouling or damage can compromise the intended path.
servicesTitle: How ICS delivers cooling tower drift control
services: Find where the water is going
Review visible carryover and the operating condition of the tower.
Inspect the eliminators
Check panels, joints, supports and seating for damage or gaps.
Clean or replace
Recommend cleaning or replacement based on the installed material and condition.
Select the right eliminator
Match replacement components to the tower arrangement and operating requirements.
Install for a tight seal
Address fit, supports and interfaces so the assembly performs as intended.
Fix related causes
Review water distribution, louvers and airflow where they contribute to the problem.
signs: Water-use changes without an operating explanation
Recurring loss after a prior repair
supportTitle: Keeping drift low after the repair
support: Inspection and maintenance should continue after replacement to identify fouling, damage and fit problems early.
process: Price alone is not the answer
decision: A replacement choice should consider the installed geometry, water distribution and airflow, not only a component label.
faq: What is drift?
Drift is liquid water entrained in the air leaving a cooling tower.
Can eliminators be repaired or cleaned?
Inspection determines whether cleaning or replacement is appropriate.
Will new eliminators solve all water loss?
Not necessarily. Other tower conditions can also contribute and should be checked.
closing: Keep treated water inside your tower.

title: Emergency Cooling Tower Repair
lead: When a cooling tower failure threatens operation, give ICS the fault, site constraints and available evidence so the repair can be scoped quickly.
overviewTitle: When a tower fails, hours matter
overview: Unexpected motor, structural or piping failures can interrupt industrial cooling. ICS assesses the condition, immediate risk and feasible repair sequence before a permanent scope is selected.
principleTitle: First steps while you wait for us
principles: Make it safe
Follow the site's own isolation and safety procedures before inspection or repair.
Gather records
Collect tower identification, operating history, drawings and photographs.
Call ICS
Explain the failure, affected cell and operational urgency so the enquiry can be scoped.
services: Motors and gearboxes
Investigate mechanical faults and the associated drive system.
Fans and drive shafts
Inspect damaged or vibrating rotating components.
Structure and fan deck
Assess damage affecting the tower's structure and access.
Casing and louvers
Repair components that affect airflow or containment.
Water distribution and piping
Locate leaks, damage and flow interruptions.
Heat-transfer components
Assess damaged fill, eliminators and related assemblies.
signsTitle: What to have ready when you call
support: An immediate repair may restore operation while a separate permanent repair or upgrade is planned. ICS can help document the remaining scope.
decision: The available shutdown window, condition of adjacent components and required duty determine whether a temporary measure or a full repair is appropriate.
faq: How fast can ICS get to my site?
Timing depends on location, access and scope. Contact ICS with the fault and site details for an assessment.
Can you replace a tower built by another manufacturer?
ICS can evaluate the existing tower and its components before recommending a repair or replacement path.
Should I keep running the tower while awaiting help?
Follow your site's safety and operating procedures; ICS cannot determine safe operation without a site-specific assessment.
closing: Cooling tower down? Contact ICS now.

title: Cooling Tower Rebuilds and New Towers
lead: Repair, rebuild or start over: compare the condition, remaining life and required duty before committing to a major tower project.
overview: A tower with widespread structural or mechanical deterioration may need more than a single component repair. ICS helps compare the repair cost, equipment life, tower lifespan and long-term operation before recommending a rebuild or new tower.
principles: Survey
Inspect structure, heat-transfer sections, drives and water distribution.
Compare
Set the scope and expected life of repair against a rebuild or replacement.
Decide
Sequence the work around site access, shutdown windows and required duty.
services: Complete structure replacement
Review worn framing, supports, casing and access components.
Wood to FRP conversion
Consider material replacement where existing wood components have deteriorated.
Fill conversion
Assess fill condition and select a suitable replacement arrangement.
Mechanical equipment upgrade
Review fans, drives, gearboxes and other worn mechanical systems.
Thermal upgrade
Determine whether the tower can meet current and future cooling requirements.
New tower and full cooling block
Compare a complete new installation with the scope of rebuilding the existing asset.
signsTitle: Signs repair has stopped paying off
signs: Repeated repairs to the same systems
support: A practical decision compares technical condition, installation constraints, shutdown impact, operating requirements and the expected life of each option.
processTitle: Four paths for an aging tower
decision: A rebuild or new tower needs a workable site sequence. ICS can discuss scope, access and timing before a project is committed.
faq: What is the difference between a rebuild and a replacement?
A rebuild retains selected parts of the existing installation; replacement introduces a new tower system. The actual scope follows inspection.
Can you rebuild a tower made by another manufacturer?
ICS can assess the installed tower and component compatibility before proposing a scope.
How long does a rebuild take?
Duration depends on the condition, selected scope, site access and shutdown constraints.
closing: Get a clear comparison before you commit budget.
